overview: The Medford Climate Equity Council reviewed upcoming community environmental events, discussed a youth employment proposal for city gardening and tree care, and received updates on municipal energy initiatives and high school sustainability goals.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The council approved the minutes from the March 2026 meeting.

items.title: Meeting Schedule
items.summary: The council maintained its next meeting date for May 20, 2026, with flexibility to adjust the schedule if needed.

items.title: Department Internships
items.summary: Brenda Pike announced that Tufts University interns will join the planning department in May to support council administration.

items.title: Community Events Review
items.summary: Council members reviewed a calendar of spring events, including local cleanups, recycling drives, swap meets, and a planned June 9 Senior Center workshop on third-party energy suppliers.

items.title: Youth Gardening and Tree Care Initiatives
items.summary: Staff outlined plans for a grant-funded youth employment program focused on raised-bed herb gardening at City Hall and volunteer tree watering with Trees Medford.

items.title: City Environmental and Energy Updates
items.summary: Brenda Pike presented updates on Electrify Medford, real-time school air quality sensors, a Tufts Park playground survey, revisions to the municipal energy aggregation plan, and LEED certification goals for the high school project.

items.title: Soil Contamination and Testing Outreach
items.summary: The council discussed raising public awareness about lead contamination in residential soil and promoting soil testing and raised-bed gardening.
